title: Micro vs Macro Explained Simply | Marketing Management Ep 6
description:
Zoya's wall is covered in notes: the farmer, Mrs. Rao, the new bakery, jaggery prices, a new food rule. Too much to think about at once, so she needs two boxes. In this animated lesson, Laddoo Lab, a tiny millet laddoo brand from a home kitchen in Bengaluru, sorts its whole world into the microenvironment and the macroenvironment.

You will see Kotler and Armstrong's definitions, the actors close to the company versus the larger societal forces that affect them, drawn as one company inside two circles. Then we follow one pack of laddoos through the microenvironment: a supplier, the company, an intermediary (the bank and UPI), the customer, a competitor and a public, with goods flowing out and money flowing back. We walk through Kotler's six macro forces, demographic, economic, natural, technological, political and cultural, each with an example and the actor it hits, including the United Nations' 2023 estimate that India had become the world's most populous country, and compare them with the PESTLE checklist. We spot micro and macro at work today in a hospital, a phone maker, an airline and a bank, and look honestly at the human side: forces overlap, lists get old, and a map shows the world but not the path.

This is Episode 6 of our Marketing Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
